t.avert.texte:
HYPNOGEN produces rhythmic flashing light. In some people, this type of stimulation can trigger an epileptic seizure, even with no known history.

  • Do not use the app if you or a family member have epilepsy, a history of convulsions or photosensitivity.
  • Avoid it without medical advice if you have migraines, a psychiatric disorder, are pregnant, or have a pacemaker.
  • Never while driving or operating machinery.
  • Stop immediately if you feel unwell, dizzy, nauseous, have blurred vision or make involuntary movements.
  • Keep headphone volume moderate.

By default, all sessions stay below 14 Hz, outside the most sensitive 15–25 Hz range: that range only opens separately, with restricted light. Never any saturated red. Tapping the screen turns the light off at once. This is not a medical device.
t.aide.principe:
How it works

HYPNOGEN flashes the screen at a given frequency while the headphones play a beat at the same frequency. Light and sound read the same clock: each flash lands on the same point of the beat, from the start to the end of the session.

You practise with your eyes closed, phone 10–15 cm from your face. Through the eyelids, rhythmic light often brings up coloured patterns, geometric shapes, sometimes more complex images: these are phosphenes, produced by the visual system itself.

A session is a series of phases. Each phase moves the frequency from a start value to an end value, smoothly (zero slope at the start and end, no jolt between two phases), or keeps it on a hold. Phases have a relative weight, not a fixed duration: if you shorten a session from 30 to 20 minutes, the whole progression tightens without losing any step.
t.aide.bandes:
Frequency bands

Sessions are described using EEG bands. These are handy landmarks: the stimulation does not “put” the brain into a state, it offers a rhythm that each person follows to some degree.

BandRangeAssociated with
Delta0.25 – 4 Hzdeep sleep
Theta4 – 8 Hzdrowsiness, edge of sleep, hypnagogic images
Alpha8 – 13 Hzrelaxed wakefulness, eyes closed
Low beta13 – 14 Hzalert wakefulness (default ceiling)
Beta15 – 25 Hzactive wakefulness, concentration. Peak photosensitive-epilepsy sensitivity: closed by default, light restricted once open
Gamma35 – 45 HzLED strip only, eyes open (40 Hz GAMMA session). Between 25 and 35 Hz the light stays off

The value 7.83 Hz, which appears in several sessions, is the frequency of the Schumann resonance. Here it serves as an anchor point at the alpha–theta boundary.
t.aide.lumiere:
Light: colours and waveforms

Sine
The light rises and falls smoothly. Enveloping, suited to relaxation and sleep sessions.
Pulse
Short, sharp, almost square flash. Richer in visual patterns, used for imagery and energising sessions.
Warm amber, amber, gold
Warm hues, the most restful. Saturated red is never shown: it is the most provocative colour for photosensitivity.
Green, violet
Cool hues, specific to MEMORY (green) and to MEDITATION and TRANCE (violet).
Sweep
The hue goes round the colour wheel in 50 seconds, always without saturated red.
t.aide.son:
Sound

Binaural
Two slightly different pure tones, one per ear (for example 197 and 203 Hz for 6 Hz). The beat does not exist in the air: it arises in the brain. Stereo headphones required.
Isochronic
A single tone, in both ears, whose volume pulses at the session's rhythm. The sound peak coincides with the flash. Also works on a speaker.
Carrier
Pitch of the base tone: 200 Hz (low, like the HYPNOGEN device), 300 or 400 Hz. The binaural beat is usually best perceived around 400 Hz; 200 Hz is gentler for sleep.

These settings are grouped in the “Sound settings” block, open on first use and then folded: its summary (sound type, carrier, volume, output) stays visible. Each setting is detailed in the next section.
t.aide.reglages:
Settings in detail

All settings are saved on the phone and restored the next time you open the app. They never leave the device.

Session

The top strip scrolls through the eleven sessions. Choosing one shows its profile (frequency curve over time) and applies its suggested duration. The red band on the profile marks the 15–25 Hz zone, which the app does not reach while the beta zone is closed. The “Full session details” link opens the detailed description of the session.

Duration

10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 45 or 60 minutes. All phases stretch or shrink in the same proportions: a shortened session keeps its progression, it just goes through it faster. Very short phases leave less time to settle in; below half the suggested duration, the effect is often weaker.

Frequency: PROFILE or MANUAL

PROFILE (default): the session drives the frequency, phase after phase.

MANUAL: you set a fixed frequency with the “Fixed” slider, from 0.5 to 14 Hz (25 Hz with the beta zone open). During the session, the −0.5 Hz and +0.5 Hz buttons change it without stopping. The session then only provides its colour and waveform. In manual mode, the personal frequency is not applied and the light in sleep sessions does not turn off by itself.

Typical use: after a FIBONACCI session, replay in manual mode the hold that gave the sharpest images.

Light

Maximum flash intensity, from 10 to 100% (70% by default). It applies on top of screen brightness, which should stay at maximum. Start at 70%; go up if the patterns stay faint, go down if the light is dazzling through your eyelids.

Depth

Gap between the flash peak and the trough between two flashes, from 30 to 100% (80% by default). At 100%, the light drops to full darkness. At 80%, the trough keeps 20% of the peak brightness. At 50%, the light only drops halfway: the flicker becomes a gentle pulse.

High depth gives more contrasted patterns; lower depth is more comfortable and more cautious. If you find the flicker tiring, lower the depth first, before the light.

Personal frequency

Shows your personal frequency if it has been measured. “Measure” starts the measurement (2 min 30 s, see the next section). “Tune alpha” turns the tuning of sessions to this frequency on or off; the button only appears after a measurement.

Volume

From 0 to 100% (55% by default). The curve is progressive: low values stay easy to fine-tune, which matters for sleep. The sound fades in over 20 seconds at the start of the session and fades out over 15 seconds at the end: do not adjust the phone volume at the very start, wait until it has risen. Keep a moderate level, especially for long sessions.

Music

From 0 to 100% (70% by default). The four meditations BREATH, TEMPLE, OCEAN and DAWN have music composed live by the app: sustained chords, singing bowls, a sparse melody and a swell, in a reverb. It never repeats exactly. Everything is tuned to the carrier, which becomes a note of every chord. In binaural mode, each note of the pad carries the same beat as the carrier, in phase with the light; bowls and melody notes land on a flash. The deeper the session goes, the darker the tone and the sparser the music. The slider sets the music against the beat; the main volume acts on both. The other sessions have no music.

Sound: BINAURAL or ISOCHRONIC

Binaural: each ear receives a slightly different pure tone; the difference between the two is the session frequency. This is the original HYPNOGEN mode. It requires stereo headphones or earphones; left/right orientation does not matter.

Isochronic: a single tone whose volume rises and falls at the session's rhythm, with the sound peak on the flash. The beat is stronger and works on a speaker, but it is also more noticeable, which can disturb sleep.

Carrier

Pitch of the base tone: 200, 300 or 400 Hz (200 Hz by default). The session frequency does not change, only the pitch does. 200 Hz is low and discreet; 400 Hz makes the binaural beat clearer for many people. Try all three on the same session and keep the one that suits you.

Audio output and calibration

Bluetooth headphones delay the sound by 100 to 300 ms depending on the model; without correction, the flash would come before the sound. Each output saves its own delay: “Wired / speaker” (0 ms by default) and “Bluetooth headphones” (180 ms by default). “Add” creates an output for another headset, starting at 180 ms.

To calibrate an output:

  1. Choose the output in the list and plug in or connect the matching headphones.
  2. Tap “Calibrate this output”. A click sounds a little more than once per second: tap the screen at the same time as each click, about a dozen times. The first two taps don't count.
  3. The screen then shows, without sound, balls dropping towards a line: tap the screen at the moment each ball crosses the line.
  4. The app works out how far the sound lags behind the picture, then flashes and clicks together. If they don't land exactly together, adjust with the slider or the −5 / +5 ms buttons: increase if the flash comes before the click, decrease if it comes after.
  5. Tap “Save”.

Tapping along is easier than judging by eye whether a flash and a click coincide, and your reaction time, the same in both steps, largely cancels out. “Set by hand” skips the measurement and goes straight to the slider. Redo the calibration if you change headphones or if the sync seems to drift. The “latency reported by the browser” is for information only: it is often wrong over Bluetooth.

Folded sound settings

Once the first setup is done, the sound block folds and shows its summary. Tap it to open it and change a setting.
t.aide.perso:
Measuring your personal frequency

The sessions are built around 10 Hz, the average value of the alpha rhythm. But each person has their own alpha peak, somewhere between about 8 and 12 Hz. The measurement looks for the frequency at which the light gives you the sharpest patterns, then shifts the sessions' alpha phases towards that value.

Preparing the measurement

  • Choose a calm moment when you are not especially tired: the frequency varies a little with alertness.
  • First set the light and depth as for a normal session.
  • Sit down, phone 10–15 cm from your face, headphones on, eyes closed.

How it goes

  1. Tap “Measure” next to “Personal frequency”.
  2. For 2 min 30 s, the amber light flashes in pulses and the frequency rises steadily from 7 to 13 Hz (the sound follows). The first three seconds are for starting up and do not count.
  3. Tap the screen each time the patterns are sharpest, most colourful or most vivid. A click confirms each tap. You can tap several times, for example at the start and end of a zone where the images are strong: this is actually recommended.
  4. Let the measurement run to the end. You can also stop it earlier: the taps already made are used.

During the measurement, a tap does not turn the light off: it marks the moment. The “Stop” button stays visible.

How the result is calculated

  • For each tap, the app takes the frequency shown 0.6 seconds earlier, to allow for your reaction time.
  • The result is the median of these frequencies: a single tap that is too early or too late does not move it.
  • It is limited to between 8 and 12 Hz, then saved, and tuning is turned on automatically.
  • With no taps, nothing changes.

What tuning does

Tuning shifts the sessions' alpha zone towards your frequency, without touching the rest:

  • at 10 Hz, the session uses exactly your frequency;
  • the correction decreases away from 10 Hz and reaches zero at 7 Hz and 13 Hz;
  • below 7 Hz (theta, delta) and above 13 Hz, nothing changes;
  • the 14 Hz ceiling is always respected.

Example with a personal frequency of 9 Hz: 10 Hz becomes 9 Hz, 8.5 Hz becomes 8 Hz, 12 Hz becomes 11.67 Hz; 7 and 13 Hz stay as they are. With 11 Hz: 10 Hz becomes 11 Hz and 12 Hz becomes 12.33 Hz.

The profile shown on the main screen includes the tuning. The profiles in this help show the original sessions. Tuning does not apply in MANUAL mode.

Tips

  • Repeat the measurement two or three times, on different days: if the results are close, the value is reliable.
  • If the results vary a lot, or if you noticed nothing clear, turn off “Tune alpha”: the original sessions work very well without it.
  • Compare with the journal: rate a few tuned and untuned sessions, then look at the difference.
t.aide.pendant:
During a session

  • The app goes full screen and the screen stays on until the end.
  • The light fades in over 8 seconds and fades out over 10 seconds at the end; the sound fades in over 20 seconds and out over 15.
  • The bottom strip shows the session, the current phase, the frequency, the time left and the screen rate in frames per second. It disappears after 4 seconds.
  • A tap anywhere turns the light off at once, the sound continues. “Resume light” turns it back on; “Stop” ends the session. On a computer, the Esc key also stops the session.
  • In MANUAL, the −0.5 Hz and +0.5 Hz buttons change the frequency live.
  • If the screen is limited to 30 frames per second (power-saving mode), a warning appears: fast flashes would be irregular.
  • After any session longer than 2 minutes, a card asks you to rate it.
t.aide.journal:
Journal and blind trials

After any session longer than 2 minutes, you rate visions and relaxation out of 10. Ratings stay on the phone and can be exported as CSV, with the session, duration, sound type, carrier, depth and tuning.

In “Blind trials” mode, one session in two is randomly given arrhythmic light: same average frequency, but irregular intervals. The sound stays rhythmic. You rate first; the condition is revealed only afterwards. After about twenty sessions, comparing the ratings shows what the rhythm really adds, for you.
t.aide.seances:
The sessions

Fifteen sessions below 14 Hz, including four meditations with music (BREATH, TEMPLE, OCEAN, DAWN), plus CONCENTRATION and GAMMA, reserved for the beta zone. The tables show the sequence for the suggested duration.
t.aide.securite:
Safety

Rhythmic flashing light: contraindicated in case of epilepsy, a history of convulsions or photosensitivity, personal or in the family. Stop at the slightest discomfort. HYPNOGEN is not a medical device and does not claim to treat any condition.
t.beta.note: Above 14 Hz: light 40% at most, depth 50% at most, sine wave, 10 min at most per session.
t.beta.texte:
The 15–25 Hz range is the peak of photosensitive-epilepsy sensitivity: it is where flashing light most easily triggers a seizure in sensitive people, sometimes with no known history.

Once the zone is open, as soon as the frequency goes above 14 Hz:

  • light is limited to 40% and depth to 50%;
  • the wave becomes a sine, even in a pulse session;
  • a session spends no more than 10 minutes above 14 Hz, then stays at 14 Hz;
  • the light turns off if the screen runs below 50 frames per second.

Do not use it when tired or short of sleep, after drinking alcohol, or with a medicine that lowers the seizure threshold. Keep your eyes closed. Tapping the screen turns the light off at once.
t.bq.1: During an HYPNOGEN session, have you ever felt unwell, had a headache, visual discomfort or a muscle jerk?
t.bq.2: Are you under 20? (Photosensitivity is most common between ages 7 and 19.)
t.beta.refus: With this answer, the beta zone stays closed.
t.beta.case: I understand this is the most sensitive range and I will stop at the slightest symptom.
t.beta.manque: The beta zone opens after {n} sessions of at least {min} minutes rated in the log. You have {k} so far.

t.hud.beta.lent: Screen below {n} frames per second: light off above 14 Hz, sound continues.
t.aide.beta:
The beta zone (15–25 Hz)

By default, HYPNOGEN never goes above 14 Hz. The 15–25 Hz range, the beta band, is also the peak of photosensitive-epilepsy sensitivity: it stays closed until you open it yourself, in Settings → Beta zone.

Conditions for opening it

  • you have accepted the general safety warning;
  • you have rated at least 3 sessions of at least 10 minutes in the log;
  • you answer no to two more questions: feeling unwell during a session, being under 20.

What changes above 14 Hz

  • Light 40% at most, depth 50% at most: the contrast of the flicker matters as much as its frequency.
  • Sine wave enforced: the sharp edges of a pulse are more provocative.
  • 10 minutes at most per session above 14 Hz; after that the session stays at 14 Hz until the end.
  • Screen at 50 frames per second or more: below that, a 20 Hz flicker breaks up into slower, irregular beats. The light turns off and the sound continues.
  • These limits come in gradually between 14 and 15 Hz: there is no step in brightness.

What it allows

The CONCENTRATION session (12 → 18.5 → 15 → 12 Hz, 20 minutes at most), MANUAL mode up to 25 Hz, and the 40 Hz GAMMA session on the LED strip (see “Strip and gamma”). Above about 20 Hz the binaural beat becomes hard to hear: prefer ISOCHRONIC sound. “Close” brings the app back below 14 Hz.

t.aide.ruban:
LED strip and gamma

The phone can drive the LED strip of the HYPNOGEN board, flashed with the HypnoGenRuban sketch. The phone keeps the interface and the sound; the board only does the light. The link is direct Bluetooth Low Energy: everything works offline, even in airplane mode with Bluetooth turned back on.

Connecting

  • Settings → LED strip → Connect, then choose HYPNOGEN-RUBAN in the list. Chrome asks for this choice every time the app is started.
  • The first time, allow Chrome to access “Nearby devices”.
  • Once connected, all the light goes through the strip and the screen stays dark. The board's indicator blinks while waiting and stays on once connected.
  • Web Bluetooth: Chrome on Android. Safari on iPhone does not offer it.

Sync and calibration

The phone does not send one command per flash: it sends the beat phase 0.8 s in advance, and the board computes the light itself, on a shared clock corrected every second (accuracy shown in Settings). The strip delay is calibrated like the screen's: with the strip connected, “Calibrate this output” replaces the ball step with strip flashes. It is stored separately for each audio output.

The GAMMA session

A 40 Hz plateau, in pulses, warm white, 15 minutes suggested, 20 at most. It requires the beta zone open and the strip connected. The sound is always isochronic (the binaural beat does not carry 40 Hz). It is done with eyes open, the strip facing a wall.

Strip safety

  • The board applies its own limits, whatever the phone asks: capped power, beta-zone restriction, light off between 25 and 35 Hz and above 45 Hz, gamma at 50% at most.
  • It derives the frequency from the phase it receives: these limits do not depend on an announced value.
  • Link lost or missing nodes: off within 0.3 s. The phone retries the connection on its own.
  • Tapping the screen turns the strip off within 30 ms, just like the screen.

t.musique.note: Pads, singing bowls and melody generated live and tuned to the carrier, in the BREATH, TEMPLE, OCEAN and DAWN meditations. At 0%, beat only.

RELAXATION.but: Gradual relaxation, from calm wakefulness to a settled state.
RELAXATION.desc: Steady descent from high alpha (12 Hz) to the theta–delta threshold (4 Hz), with no detour: each phase starts exactly where the previous one ends. The last phase holds 4 Hz to give you time to settle into the calm reached.
RELAXATION.ressenti: Gradual letting go, breathing slows down. As the frequency drops, the flashes seem broader and slower, the patterns wider.
RELAXATION.conseil: The simplest session to discover HYPNOGEN. In the evening, to switch off after work, sitting or lying down.

IMAGINATION.but: Daydreaming and mental images, with sharp flashes.
IMAGINATION.desc: Sharp pulses and a slowly turning hue (one trip round the colour wheel in 50 s). The frequency descends from alpha to 6 Hz, well into theta, then settles there for the longest phase of the session.
IMAGINATION.ressenti: This is the session richest in images: geometric patterns, tunnels, shifting colours, sometimes more complex scenes in the last quarter.
IMAGINATION.conseil: Do not try to hold on to the images: let them come and go. Light at 70% or more, high depth. Note your visions in the journal to compare from one time to the next.

HYPNAGOGIE.but: Long hold at 7.83 Hz to stay on the edge of sleep.
HYPNAGOGIE.desc: After a short descent, a long hold at 7.83 Hz takes up nearly half the session, at the alpha–theta boundary. The end slides down to 6.3 Hz. The aim is to stay suspended on the edge of falling asleep, without tipping over.
HYPNAGOGIE.ressenti: A floating feeling, thoughts coming apart, brief hypnagogic images that appear and fade. The body may feel heavy or, on the contrary, light.
HYPNAGOGIE.conseil: Sitting or half-lying is best: lying flat, it is easy to fall asleep. If you fall asleep every time, shorten to 20 min or switch to MANUAL at around 8 Hz.

ENDORMISSEMENT.but: Continuous descent into delta, ending in darkness, to fall asleep.
ENDORMISSEMENT.desc: Continuous descent from 10 Hz to 0.25 Hz. The light fades out around 2 Hz: the end of the session takes place in darkness, with the sound alone continuing the descent into delta.
ENDORMISSEMENT.ressenti: Gradual drowsiness. Many people do not see the end of the session.
ENDORMISSEMENT.conseil: In bed, phone on a holder, headphones comfortable enough to sleep in, low volume. The sound fades out, and the screen then goes to sleep as usual.

RÊVE.but: Slow slide towards deep sleep, ending in darkness.
RÊVE.desc: Starts already low, at 8 Hz, then slides more slowly and for longer than FALLING ASLEEP into delta, down to 0.25 Hz. As with that session, the light goes out around 2 Hz and the sound continues alone.
RÊVE.ressenti: A gentle dive, without the alpha phase at the start: suits you when you are already tired.
RÊVE.conseil: For a nap, bedtime, or after waking in the night. Same precautions as for FALLING ASLEEP: sleep headphones, low volume.

ANCRAGE.but: Short refocusing session that ends very low.
ANCRAGE.desc: Short session: a hold at 7.83 Hz to settle, then a steep descent to 1.12 Hz, held until the end.
ANCRAGE.ressenti: A clean break from the agitation of the moment; the very slow ending leaves a calm, heavy state.
ANCRAGE.conseil: Midday break. The session ends very low: allow two or three minutes to come back before resuming an activity, and never right before driving.

MÉDITATION.but: Long meditation, slow descent towards 1 Hz.
MÉDITATION.desc: The longest descent into light delta: alpha, a hold at 7.83 Hz, then three successive slides down to 1.05 Hz, held for the last phase. Violet, sine wave.
MÉDITATION.ressenti: Deep calm, attention settling without effort. The light becomes very slow and enveloping in the last third.
MÉDITATION.conseil: Sitting, back straight, following your breath if you are used to it. 30 min suggested; 20 min is enough to start.

TRANSE.but: Deep dive, then a rise back to theta.
TRANSE.desc: Pulsed descent to a long hold at 2 Hz, then a rise to 4 Hz to end in theta. The way back up brings images back after the deepest phase.
TRANSE.ressenti: A deep, empty phase in the middle, then images reappear, often sharper than at the start.
TRANSE.conseil: An intense session: keep it for when you tolerate the others well. Lying down, with nothing scheduled afterwards.

MÉMOIRE.but: Alternating alpha and theta, back to a lively alpha.
MÉMOIRE.desc: Alternates between alpha (10.2 Hz) and theta (7.8 Hz) with a hold on each, then returns to a lively alpha. Green, sine wave. The session never goes below 7.8 Hz.
MÉMOIRE.ressenti: Relaxation without drowsiness; you come out of it awake.
MÉMOIRE.conseil: Before or during a break from studying or thinking. It is designed to go with that moment; no effect on memory is promised.

HUMEUR.desc: Energising session that rises from 10 to 14 Hz, holds at the top, then comes back down to 12 Hz. Gold, pulses. Capped at 14 Hz, whereas the protocols it draws on go up to 16 Hz: the margin keeps the session out of the sensitive zone.
HUMEUR.ressenti: Rather stimulating, bright and fast flashes.
HUMEUR.conseil: In the morning or early afternoon, sitting; not in the evening. If the flicker is uncomfortable, lower the depth to 50–60%.

FIBONACCI.but: Holds at 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 13 Hz, then back.
FIBONACCI.desc: Eleven equal holds following the Fibonacci sequence, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 13 Hz, then back down. Transitions from one hold to the next are smoothed over 150 ms. The sequence stops at 13 Hz: the next term, 21 Hz, would fall in the excluded range.
FIBONACCI.ressenti: An exploration session: each hold has its own character, from single flashes at 1 Hz to the fast flicker at 13 Hz.
FIBONACCI.conseil: Useful for finding the frequencies that work best for you. Note in the journal which hold gave the sharpest images, then try that frequency in MANUAL.

CONCENTRATION.but: A climb into beta for alertness and attention. Beta zone.
CONCENTRATION.desc: Starts in high alpha (12 Hz), rises smoothly to a plateau at 18.5 Hz, comes back down through 15 Hz and ends on a 12 Hz plateau to return to calm wakefulness. Green, sine wave. This is the firmware session that is disabled on the hardware unit; here, above 14 Hz, the light is restricted (40%, depth 50%) and the duration is limited to 20 minutes, to stay under 10 minutes of beta.
CONCENTRATION.ressenti: Rather bright and stimulating: the fast flicker melts into a shimmer, with few structured images.
CONCENTRATION.conseil: Only try it once the other sessions are well tolerated, sitting, in the morning or early afternoon. Prefer ISOCHRONIC sound: above 15 Hz the binaural beat is hard to hear. Stop at the slightest headache.

GAMMA.but: A 40 Hz plateau on the LED strip, eyes open. Beta zone.
GAMMA.desc: A single 40 Hz plateau, in pulses, warm white, with isochronic sound at the same frequency. The session starts directly at 40 Hz with a light fade-in: it never crosses the 15–35 Hz range. Light limited to 50%, 20 minutes at most. It only runs on the LED strip.
GAMMA.ressenti: The light does not clearly flash: it seems to vibrate or shimmer. The sound is like a fast hum.
GAMMA.conseil: Eyes open, strip facing a wall, sitting in a dimly lit room. Studies on 40 Hz stimulation are research work: no effect is promised. Stop at the slightest headache.

SOUFFLE.but: Breath-guided meditation, six breaths per minute, with music.
SOUFFLE.desc: Guided breathing at six cycles per minute (4 s in, 6 s out): the music swells as you breathe in and ebbs as you breathe out, like a swell, and the light breathes with it. The frequency stays in alpha, from 10 to 8.5 Hz, slides towards 7 Hz for the central part, then rises back to 8.5 Hz to finish clear. Turquoise, sine wave; major chords, sparse melody.
SOUFFLE.ressenti: After a few cycles your breathing settles on the swell by itself. Steady calm, without drowsiness, with a soft, enveloping light.
SOUFFLE.conseil: The best way into the music meditations. Sitting, shoulders relaxed: breathe in through the nose as the sound rises, breathe out slowly as it falls, without forcing. 15 min suggested; any time of day.

TEMPLE.but: Descent into theta to the sound of singing bowls.
TEMPLE.desc: A deep modal drone, minor chords that change slowly, and singing bowls struck every 15 to 30 seconds, each on a flash, ringing for a long time. The frequency goes from 10 Hz to a hold at 7.83 Hz, descends to a long hold at 4.5 Hz, deep in theta, then rises back to 6 Hz. Indigo, sine wave.
TEMPLE.ressenti: Each bowl gives attention something to rest on; between strikes, the inner silence widens. The 4.5 Hz hold is often rich in slow, blurred images.
TEMPLE.conseil: For a 25-minute seated meditation, back straight. If your mind wanders, simply come back at the next bowl. Headphones recommended: in binaural mode the pad also carries the beat.

OCÉAN.but: Slow dive into deep theta, rocked by the swell.
OCÉAN.desc: A continuous swell, deep dark chords lasting a minute each, rare distant bowls. The frequency descends from 10 to 3.5 Hz, at the theta–delta boundary, holds there for the longest phase, then rises back to 5 Hz so as not to finish at the lowest point. Blue, sine wave. The music darkens and thins out as you go down.
OCÉAN.ressenti: A feeling of immersion and floating, sometimes of losing track of the body. Few clear images: rather a calm, dense emptiness.
OCÉAN.conseil: Lying down or well supported, 30 minutes, with nothing scheduled afterwards. The session goes low: take two or three minutes to come back before getting up, and never before driving.

AURORE.but: Rising meditation, from theta to clear alpha, with luminous music.
AURORE.desc: The reverse path of the other meditations: start in theta at 6 Hz, then a gradual rise to 10.5 Hz, held at the end of the session. Gold, sine wave. Lydian chords that brighten, a melody more and more present as the frequency rises, regular bowls.
AURORE.ressenti: You start from an inward state and gradually return to a calm, sharp wakefulness with a clear mind. The music becomes brighter and livelier as the session goes on.
AURORE.conseil: In the morning, on waking or before starting the day, or to close a deep session. Sitting. 20 min suggested.
